title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: During account registration, the Homeowner provides identified personal data (name, email, contact information) which is processed by the Home Hub. This creates a direct link between the data subject and their personal information.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identification information

title: Unique identifiers in device enrollment
description: Camera and sensor enrollment involves unique device identifiers that can be linked back to the Homeowner's account, creating persistent identification references.
assumptions: Devices have unique identifiers that are registered to the account

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The Home Hub can link all registered devices and account data through unique identifiers (account ID, device serial numbers), enabling comprehensive data association across the system.
assumptions: System maintains identifier-based linking between account and devices

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: The combination of account data and enrolled device types/locations can be analyzed to create profiles about the Homeowner's lifestyle, security preferences, and home layout.
assumptions: Device enrollment data includes location/type information that can be profiled

title: Excessive data type sensitivity in registration
description: Registration may collect more sensitive personal data than functionally required for basic account creation and device enrollment (e.g., full address, phone number when email might suffice).
assumptions: Registration form collects multiple data fields beyond minimum necessary
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific registration form design

title: Extended data retention during registration
description: Registration and enrollment data may be retained longer than functionally needed, especially if no clear data retention policy exists for account and device information.
assumptions: System retains registration data indefinitely without clear retention limits

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected during registration and device enrollment, including metadata, device identifiers, and how this data will be used.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not comprehensively explain all data processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: Homeowner may lack granular control over which personal data is collected during registration and how it is processed, with limited preference settings available.
assumptions: Registration process offers limited or no data processing preferences

title: Attributable registration data
description: Registration and enrollment actions create data records that can be attributed to the Homeowner, preventing them from denying these account creation and device enrollment actions.
assumptions: System maintains logs of registration and enrollment activities

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If registration collects more personal data than necessary for account creation and device enrollment, this may violate GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Registration form may collect excessive data fields
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices

title: Profiling through video content analysis
description: Video clips uploaded from the Home Hub can be analyzed to profile individuals based on their activities, movements, and behaviors captured in the footage.
assumptions: Video content contains recognizable individuals and their activities

title: Linking through unique identifiers in video metadata
description: Video clips may contain unique identifiers (device IDs, user IDs, timestamps) in metadata that enable linking data across the cloud storage system.
assumptions: Video files include metadata with unique identifiers

title: Processing of identified data in video clips
description: The Home Hub processes video clips that contain identified information such as faces, license plates, and other personally identifiable visual data.
assumptions: Camera captures identifiable individuals and objects

title: Revealing attributes in stored video
description: Stored video clips contain revealing attributes (facial features, clothing, location context) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Video quality is sufficient for identification

title: Video as attributable data evidence
description: Video clips can be used as evidence to attribute actions, presence, or activities to specific individuals, preventing them from denying such claims.
assumptions: Video content is clear enough to identify individuals and their actions

title: Sensitive video data type collection
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than functionally required, especially if all footage is stored regardless of content.
assumptions: All recorded video is uploaded without filtering for sensitivity

title: Extended video retention duration
description: Video clips may be stored in cloud storage longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risks over time.
assumptions: Retention policies may not align with functional requirements

title: Third-party cloud provider access
description: Personal video data is made accessible to cloud storage provider as a predetermined party, which may exceed what is functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud provider has access to stored video data

title: Unawareness of video recording and upload
description: Individuals captured in video clips may be unaware that their personal data is being recorded by the Home Hub and uploaded to cloud storage.
assumptions: No clear notification to individuals being recorded

title: Limited control over video data erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to request rectification or erasure of their personal data in video clips once uploaded to cloud storage.
assumptions: Limited mechanisms for data subject rights enforcement

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing all video clips in cloud storage may process more personal data than actually needed for the system's functional goals.
assumptions: No filtering or selective storage of video content

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Video clips may be stored longer than necessary, violating GDPR storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: Retention periods may not be clearly defined or enforced

title: Motion pattern profiling
description: Real-time motion alerts from the Home Hub can be analyzed to profile individual behavior patterns, such as daily routines, presence/absence schedules, and movement patterns within the home.
assumptions: Motion data contains sufficient temporal and spatial detail to enable behavioral profiling

title: Revealing presence attributes
description: Motion alert data reveals revealing attributes about data subjects including when they are present at home, their movement patterns, and potentially which areas of the home they occupy.
assumptions: Motion sensors can distinguish between different individuals or at minimum reveal occupancy patterns

title: Sensitive motion data collection
description: Motion data is highly sensitive as it reveals intimate details about home occupancy, daily routines, and personal behavior patterns that should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Motion data is considered sensitive personal data under privacy regulations

title: Excessive frequency of motion data processing
description: Real-time motion alerts mean personal data is processed more frequently than may be functionally needed, creating continuous surveillance of home activity.
assumptions: Real-time transmission is required for the alert functionality

title: Implicit presence disclosure
description: Motion alerts implicitly disclose presence/absence patterns as a side-effect of the explicit motion detection functionality, revealing when individuals are home or away.
assumptions: Motion detection inherently reveals occupancy information

title: Unawareness of motion tracking
description: Data subjects may be unaware that their motion patterns are being continuously tracked, recorded, and transmitted to the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Users may not fully understand the extent of motion data collection

title: Lack of motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how motion data is processed, including frequency, granularity, and retention.
assumptions: System may not provide granular consent options for motion data

title: Data minimization violation
description: Real-time motion alert processing may violate the data minimization principle by collecting and processing more personal data than actually needed for the alert functionality.
assumptions: Less frequent or less granular motion data could achieve the same alert purpose
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific system requirements and whether real-time is truly necessary

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications can reveal patterns about when the homeowner is present or absent from their property. Over time, this data can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's daily routines, travel patterns, and occupancy habits.
assumptions: The backend stores or processes motion detection events that can be correlated over time

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes identified data to route motion detection notifications to the specific homeowner's device. This requires maintaining a link between the notification and the homeowner's identity.
assumptions: The system uses user accounts or device identifiers to deliver notifications

title: Sensitive occupancy data disclosure
description: Motion detection notifications inherently disclose sensitive information about property occupancy. This reveals when the homeowner is home or away, which could be considered highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: Motion detection data is treated as personal data under applicable privacy regulations

title: Excessive notification frequency
description: If motion detection triggers notifications frequently (e.g., every motion event), this could constitute excessive processing of personal data beyond what is functionally needed for security awareness.
assumptions: The system may send notifications for every motion event without aggregation or filtering
uncertainty_note: Depends on system configuration - may be configurable

title: Lack of notification preference control
description: The homeowner may lack control over notification preferences such as when to receive alerts, what triggers them, or how frequently they are sent. This limits the data subject's ability to customize their privacy experience.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular notification settings
uncertainty_note: Depends on app implementation - many apps do provide settings

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: If notifications include more information than necessary (e.g., exact timestamps, location details, or motion intensity) beyond what is needed to alert the homeowner, this could violate the data minimization principle.
assumptions: The notification content may include unnecessary details
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification content design

title: Quasi-identifier linking through aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain quasi-identifiers (e.g., device type, usage patterns, time patterns) that, when combined with other data sources, could be used to link data back to specific individuals.
assumptions: Aggregated analytics may not be sufficiently anonymized to prevent re-identification through quasi-identifiers

title: Individual profiling through device usage patterns
description: Device-usage analytics can be analyzed to create behavioral profiles of individual users based on their app usage patterns, device interactions, and activity timing.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient granularity to enable individual profiling

title: Quasi-identifiers in analytics data
description: The analytics data may contain combinations of attributes (device characteristics, usage frequency, session duration, etc.) that are unique to individual data subjects.
assumptions: Analytics data includes multiple attributes that could serve as quasi-identifiers

title: Data propagation to external vendor
description: Personal data in the form of device-usage analytics is being propagated to an external cloud analytics vendor where it may not be functionally necessary for the core app functionality.
assumptions: Analytics sharing is for business purposes rather than core functionality

title: Data shared with predetermined external party
description: Device-usage analytics are shared with a predetermined cloud analytics vendor, exposing personal data to an external party beyond the mobile app backend.
assumptions: The cloud analytics vendor is a known, fixed third party

title: User unawareness of analytics data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being collected and shared with an external cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly disclose third-party analytics sharing

title: Lack of user control over analytics processing
description: Data subjects may lack the ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their device-usage analytics are processed and shared with the cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for analytics sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external vendor may process more personal data than is actually needed for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: Analytics sharing may exceed what is necessary for app operation

title: Invalid consent for third-party data sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing for analytics sharing may not rely on valid, informed consent from data subjects regarding the external vendor.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not adequately inform users about third-party analytics sharing

title: Video data contains sensitive personal information
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may contain highly sensitive personal data (faces, activities, property details) that exceeds what is functionally required for simple playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content includes identifiable personal information about homeowners and their property

title: Video data accessible to mobile app backend
description: Personal video data is made accessible to the mobile app backend process, which may be more parties than functionally necessary for the playback functionality.
assumptions: The mobile app backend is a separate system component that processes video data

title: Video content reveals identifying attributes
description: Video clips may contain revealing attributes (faces, license plates, distinctive features) that support identification of data subjects beyond what is needed for playback.
assumptions: Video content includes visual information that can identify individuals

title: Video playback patterns enable individual profiling
description: Analysis of which video clips are retrieved and when can be used to profile homeowner behavior and patterns, linking data to specific individuals.
assumptions: Video retrieval metadata is logged and can be analyzed for patterns

title: Homeowners unaware of video processing details
description: Data subjects (homeowners) may not be fully aware of how their video data is being processed, stored, and retrieved by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain video data processing flows

title: Limited control over video data retention and deletion
description: Homeowners may lack control to rectify or erase video data that is no longer relevant, particularly regarding retention periods in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video deletion/retention controls may not be user-configurable

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing full video clips may violate GDPR data minimization if less granular data (e.g., thumbnails, metadata only) could achieve the same playback functionality.
assumptions: Full video retrieval is required for playback functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether video content is strictly necessary for the stated functionality

title: Insufficient data subject controls for video data
description: GDPR requires data subject rights including access, rectification, and erasure which may not be adequately supported for video data in this flow.
assumptions: Video data management may not include comprehensive data subject rights mechanisms
